title: Proverbs 24
paragraphs: ¹ Do not envy the wicked or desire their company, ² for their hearts plot violence, and their lips speak trouble. ³ By wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established; ⁴ through knowledge its rooms are filled with rare and beautiful treasures. ⁵ A wise warrior is full of strength, and a person of knowledge increases their power.

⁶ For victory you need wise guidance, and in the abundance of counselors there is safety. ⁷ Wisdom is beyond the reach of a fool; they have nothing to say in the gate. ⁸ Whoever schemes to do evil will be known as a troublemaker. ⁹ The schemes of the foolish are sinful, and people hate a mocker. ¹⁰ If you fail in a time of trouble, how small is your strength!

¹¹ Rescue those being led away to death; hold back those stumbling toward slaughter. ¹² If you say, "But we knew nothing about this" — does not he who weighs the heart perceive it? Does not he who guards your life know it? Will he not repay everyone according to what they have done? ¹³ Eat honey, my son, for it is good; honey from the comb is sweet to your taste. ¹⁴ Know that wisdom is like honey for your soul: if you find it, there is a future hope, and your hope will not be cut off.

¹⁵ Do not lurk like an outlaw at the home of a righteous person; do not raid their dwelling place. ¹⁶ For though the righteous fall seven times, they rise again, but the wicked stumble in times of calamity. ¹⁷ Do not gloat when your enemy falls; when they stumble, do not let your heart rejoice, ¹⁸ or the LORD will see and disapprove and turn his wrath away from them. ¹⁹ Do not fret because of evildoers or envy the wicked, ²⁰ for the evildoer has no future hope, and the lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.

²¹ Fear the LORD and the king, my son, and do not join with rebellious officials, ²² for calamity will rise suddenly against them, and who knows what ruin they can bring? ²³ These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judging is not good. ²⁴ Whoever says to the guilty, "You are innocent," will be cursed by peoples and denounced by nations. ²⁵ But it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come on them.

²⁶ An honest answer is like a kiss on the lips. ²⁷ Prepare your work outside and get your fields ready; after that, build your house. ²⁸ Do not testify against your neighbor without cause; would you use your lips to deceive? ²⁹ Do not say, "I will do to them as they have done to me; I will pay them back for what they did." ³⁰ I went past the field of a sluggard, past the vineyard of someone who has no sense.

³¹ Thorns had grown up everywhere, the ground was covered with weeds, and the stone wall was in ruins. ³² I applied my heart to what I observed and learned a lesson from what I saw: ³³ A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest — ³⁴ and poverty will come on you like a thief, and scarcity like an armed man.
